topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Biology and Course Framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the course structure, central themes, and learning outcomes for understanding cancer biology.

topics.label: Biological Mechanisms and In Vitro Modeling of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how genetic and epigenetic changes disrupt normal developmental differentiation and tissue architecture, alongside the experimental considerations of studying tumor cells in culture.

topics.label: Benign and Malignant Tumor Progression, Invasion, and Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the biological distinction, histological indicators, and stepwise progression from benign precursor lesions to invasive and metastatic malignancies.

topics.label: Tumor Classification and Nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic defines the standard naming conventions and notable exceptions used to classify benign and malignant tumors by tissue of origin.

topics.label: Pathophysiological Causes of Cancer Morbidity and Mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the anatomical, metabolic, and systemic mechanisms through which local and metastatic tumors cause clinical complications and death.

topics.label: Cancer Incidence Across Tissues and Animal Species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the frequency and distribution of tumor types in human populations and across diverse multicellular animal species.

topics.label: Clinical Detection and Cancer Screening Methods
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics assess early clinical signs of cancer and the effectiveness, histological methods, and trade-offs of screening programs across different tumor types.

topics.label: Conclusion and Learning Outcomes Review
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by reiterating the core learning outcomes and looking forward to subsequent practical sessions.
